# A half-total-mass moment-interval length selector can choose a bad base

For a mixed interval measure `mu`, write `M=mu(S)` and `t=M/2`. At an integer
base j for which it is feasible, define the balanced moment interval

    M_t(j)={ (1/t)integral x f dmu : 0<=f<=1,
             integral f dmu=t, integral(z-j)f dmu=0 }.

The selector considered here chooses a base maximizing the interval's length
and then chooses its midpoint. The following exact example has a unique
maximizing base, positive-length moment intervals, and a selected point whose
actual ambient halfspace depth is strictly less than1/4.

## 1. Actual convex body and mass

Take integer fibers at `-1,0,1`:

    K_-1=[-347/400,337/400],
    K_0 =[-1/2,1/2],
    K_1 =[-53/400,43/400].

Let C be their convex hull. Their lengths and endpoint-fiber centers are

    a=171/100,  b=1,  c=6/25,  e=-1/80.

The lower-endpoint midpoint of the two outer fibers is exactly `-1/2`;
the upper-endpoint midpoint is `19/40<=1/2`. Thus their midpoint interval
is contained in K_0, and C has exactly the displayed integer fibers. It is
an ambient convex body, with all three fiber lengths positive. Its mass and
prescribed source mass are

    M=59/20,   t=59/40.

## 2. Both moment-interval endpoints are optimized exactly

For base j=0, any feasible source has equal outer masses ell and middle mass
`t-2ell`. The allowed interval is

    19/80 <=ell<=6/25.                                 (1)

For fixed fiber masses, the maximal x moment comes from each upper interval
piece, and the minimal moment comes from each lower interval piece. This is
the elementary threshold exchange: transferring selected mass upward raises
its first moment, until the selected part is an upper interval of the
prescribed length. It is valid for arbitrary densities0<=f<=1, not merely
indicator sources.

Put

    Delta_u=2u_0-u_-1-u_1=1/20,
    Delta_l=l_-1+l_1-2l_0=0.

After removing terms independent of ell, maximization of the upper moment
and maximization of the negative lower moment are respectively

    (2t-Delta_u)ell-3ell^2,
    (2t-Delta_l)ell-3ell^2.                            (2)

Their derivatives are strictly positive on (1): at its right endpoint they
are `73/50` and `151/100`. Hence BOTH are uniquely maximized at `ell=c=6/25`.
The middle retained mass is then `q=t-2c=199/200`.

The interval of resulting centroids has midpoint

    y=(2ce)/t=-6/1475,

and length

    L_0=[c(a-c)+q(1-q)]/t=14311/59000.

Equivalently its exact endpoints are

    M_t(0)=[-14791/118000,13831/118000].                 (3)

These formulas optimize over ALL admissible dominated balanced sources.

At base j=-1, the base moment condition forces the entire source onto that
single extreme fiber. Because `a>t`, its moment interval is

    M_t(-1)=[-13/100,21/200],
    L_-1=a-t=47/200.

At base j=1, the analogous condition would force all mass onto K_1, whose
mass c is less than t, so that base is infeasible. Finally,

    L_0-L_-1=223/29500>0.                              (4)

Thus the selector has a UNIQUE maximizing base j=0 and returns `(0,y)`.
There is no tie or degenerate interval ambiguity in this example.

## 3. An actual bad closed ambient cap

The cap

    H={x-z<=-6/1475}

contains the selected point on its boundary. At z=-1 it is strictly empty,
since `y-1<-347/400`; at z=1 it captures the entire fiber, since
`y+1>43/400`. At z=0 it retains the lower interval from `-1/2` to y. Its
actual mixed length is therefore

    mu(H)=c+1/2+y=2171/2950,
    M/4-mu(H)=37/23600>0.                              (5)

Nonvertical boundary intersections are points in the fibers and carry zero
mixed length, so these are exact closed-cap masses.

This falsifies the unrestricted length-maximizing selector at EXACTLY half
of the ORIGINAL total mass. It is different from the earlier `D_j/2`
selector failure.

There is a substantive limitation to this counterexample. The left fiber
is heavy (`a>M/2`) and its base is the unique weighted integer median.
Base0 has closed marginal depth `1+c=31/25<t`. Thus requiring marginal
median eligibility changes the selector and avoids this particular bad
base. No failure of that modified selector is asserted here.

## 4. The degenerate edge case for the definition

For the sharp two-fiber product `[0,1]x[0,1]`, one has M=2,t=1. At either
integer base0 or1, balance forces all source mass onto that unit interval,
so both moment bodies are SINGLETONS at its ordinary midpoint. All eligible
lengths are therefore zero. A formulation in terms of a positive-volume John
ellipsoid would be undefined there; a formulation in terms of the midpoint
of a possibly degenerate interval remains defined. Both resulting points
have exact mixed depth1/4, so this edge case is not itself a counterexample.
